scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A fridge keeps food cold. But put your hand behind it, and it's warm. That's the secret.

scenes.name: idea
scenes.text: A fridge doesn't make cold. It moves heat out of the inside, and dumps it into your kitchen.

scenes.name: evap
scenes.text: A liquid called refrigerant flows through pipes inside. It boils at a very low temperature, and as it evaporates, it soaks up heat.

scenes.name: comp
scenes.text: The compressor, that humming motor, squeezes the gas. Squeezing makes it hot, hotter than your kitchen.

scenes.name: cond
scenes.text: Coils at the back let that heat escape into the room. The gas cools down, and turns back into liquid.

scenes.name: valve
scenes.text: Then it passes through a tiny valve. The pressure drops suddenly, and it becomes icy cold again.

scenes.name: thermo
scenes.text: A thermostat switches the compressor on and off, to hold the inside at around three to five degrees.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Evaporate, squeeze, release, expand. Heat out, cold in. Follow for more on how things really work.
